rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.

Separately grep -inE '\\bleverag(e|es|ing)\\b' over body → 0 hits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body-view grep ritual_ceremony '\\b(ritual|rituals|ceremony|ceremonies)\\b' → 0 body hits (CLEAN, planted_proof true). Additional grep -inE '\\bpractice' over body → 0 hits, so the AE101 sparingly-OK practice(n) carve-out is moot; nothing to weigh.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body-view grep session_biography '\\b(caught live|now fixed|previously|used to say|MOVED)\\b' → 0 body hits; dated_line '\\b20\\d\\d-\\d\\d-\\d\\d\\b' → 0 body hits (both CLEAN, planted_proof true), so body (L1-109) carries no journey-narration at all. Maintainer block (L110-115) is present-tense standing constraint ('A skill earns its place here by becoming a check...do not broaden it back'), no transition verb. Below the maintainer cut, the <!-- backing --> block's Claims/Sources/Frameworks/Stance/OODA sections (L116-167) are the canonical backing-format.md research ledger, not ad hoc changelog: the rule's own carve-out blesses 'an empirical finding that would otherwise be re-derived' (e.g. merge-base example), and the Stance section's verification-history narrative ('Nine verified clean, two failed, one was right all along') exists precisely so a future /lecture-ooda pass does not re-doubt settled claims or re-try exhausted routes — the same shape as the blessed example. Harm this rule guards against (changelog cruft reaching a reader) is absent: backing blocks sit below the maintainer cut and never render to a student or trainer view. The new L172 note ('Declined at the 2026-09-03 polish pass: headers 4 and 5 stay declarative...Judges should not re-file') is a dated standing accept-note (name + rule cite + forward instruction), not a journey verb ('was changed', 'restored', 'used to be') — matches the sanctioned maintainer-note pattern used throughout the corpus.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 15 '##' headers (L7,11,19,29,35,43,49,55,61,69,75,83,89,95,102) against their section's actual claim. 'Stripe bets on the sandbox, not the slice' (L35) accurately reflects the body's devbox-isolation mechanism contrasted with Intercom's risk-tier slice two paragraphs earlier. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: (a) Empty negation: header 1's 'not a gate to pass' (L7) and header 3's 'not the slice' (L35) each negate a real, just-established prior (CI-as-gate; slice-based auto-merge described for Intercom immediately above), not a strawman. (b) Deictic drumroll: grep -inE 'that is the|this is the' over body → 0 hits. (c) Bold-label echo: bolded practitioner leads ('**Klaassen at Every**', '**Cherny on Claude Code**', etc.) each introduce a new predicate, never restate the bolded name as the sentence's echoed subject. (d) Citation/appendix duplication: the three 'Sources: moves N and M' sections (L89-108) are bare name+link entries, no repeated inline gloss.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'Six moves recur in the engineers running it best' (L5) names a count at a point where none of the six numbered sections is yet visible (Slides layout chunks each '##' as its own slide, so the six are never simultaneously on-screen) — matches the rule's own memory-handle carve-out ('does the numeral appear where the items are NOT visible? Yes → keep it'), not the banned adjacent-to-a-visible-list case. 'Two proofs the loop compounds' (L11) is itself a '##' header numeral, explicitly exempt per the rule ('A numeral in a `##` header is NOT covered by this rule'). 'Two different orgs, two different bets on where to put the human and where to put the silicon' (L39) performs a contrastive synthesis (naming the axis: human vs. silicon placement) rather than tallying a visible bulleted list.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE '\\bonly\\b|\\balways\\b|\\bnever\\b|nothing else|the one thing that' over body → two hits, both scoped/hedged: L47 'almost never' (hedged, not an absolute claim), L53 'run only those' sits inside a quoted question to Claude, scoped to a stated 80/20 heuristic rather than an assertion about how the world works. 'The best' (recurring rhetorical subject across all six moves) is not one of the rule's enumerated superlative words and functions as shorthand for 'the best engineers', not a falsifiable universal claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.

L57's three-sentence run ('A skill is a verifier-in-waiting. Each skill you author catches a pattern. That pattern is what your next PR's review...needs to see.') builds a chain where each sentence adds new content rather than restating the same claim at a different altitude. L85's 'The shift is not conceptual...The shift is what each move makes possible...' is negation-then-definition (rule 19's sanctioned empty-negation shape), not the same claim repeated twice. No widening qualifier ('or context-dependent', 'or rule') or duplicate second-announcement of one coinage found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.

L67: object='your own `~/.claude/skills/`' (the student's own artifact, not a generated account of it — the rule's own 'the diff is fine because the diff is the artifact' exemption), tell='a skill that catches something your CI doesn't' (concrete). Notice which hat caught what.' asks the student to compare four Claude-GENERATED review outputs against each other (a pattern-noticing task explicitly named the section's whole point at L21, 'Read the pattern across findings, not the lines'), not to manually verify a code diff for correctness — outside this rule's banned shape.

The repeated '[Org]'s own numbers' qualifier (L15, L23, L33, L37) is not NVA — it changes how the reader should weight each figure (self-report skepticism), which is a decision-relevant epistemic flag, not trivia. No purely administrative aside, no maintainer-reasoning leak, no obvious-to-a-working-engineer filler sentence found on full read.

Notice which hat caught what.' is followed by concrete follow-on direction (compare across four generated reviews for a specialisation pattern, with 'That's a panel.' naming the payoff), satisfying the rule's own carve-out ('specific column/row for next decision fine when load-bearing for what follows; ban is on generic "read it" with no follow-on'). (a) 'The loop at your desk is the one this training closed' (L85) has 'The loop at your desk' — the student's own artifact — as the sentence's head subject, with 'this training closed [it]' as an embedded relative clause, not a leading training-as-subject value-prop sentence. (L87) are concrete do-this-now imperatives in the file's own established 'Try this Monday' register, not vague coach-register vigilance-imperatives ('watch for X'). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'typing |type in|say to Claude|tell it to' over body → 0 hits. Every directed message to Claude uses 'ask Claude' plus a quoted question (L17, L27, L41, L53) — the sanctioned addressee-invocation verb per this rule's own sibling (check_writing/check_student_facing rule 21's calibration example, 'Ask Claude to review the session'), not a physical-act verb ('typing', 'saying') narrating the mechanics of sending the message.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The closing section (L83-87, 'Where this fits in your AE101 arc') is this supplementary's own bridge/close-equivalent (there is no other bridge section in a supplementary's file shape) and does genuine synthesis work — explicitly connecting the six external practitioner moves back to what the reader already built in M6 — rather than merely narrating what a later beat will cover. Deletion test: removing L85-86 would delete the file's whole payoff (why an outside practitioner survey matters to this specific reader), so the passage is not NVA cartography. The opening thesis 'Six moves recur in the engineers running it best' (L5) makes a substantive claim (what is true of top engineers), functioning as this file's Big-Idea-equivalent ('what the module earns'), not a bare forward-map of section topics ('where it sits').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Rough-cut drafts for articles.
Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL.
A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session.
One doc per scarce-attention audience; delta-only.
Trainer-facing text is self-contained.
Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
Golden path only in body.
Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module.
Simulation personas never alone.
Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
Inline links use target's title, never filename.
Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
No meta-ask when student has already decided.
`.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
Four sharing strategies (Agents 101 M7 canonical) — use verbatim.
Agents 101 M2+ Debrief — canonical shape.
Trust the prompt over the scaffold.
Mood is a design constraint, not a garnish.
Exercise headers pass the build-squint test.
No placeholders inside fences.
Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
Installed Skills invoke by name, never path.
Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
Chained-prompt isolation — don't leak downstream pipeline.
No session-resets mid-phase.
Multi-sample methods need structural enforcement.
Markdown shout (`**bold**`, `*italic*`) inside fenced prompts = dead weight in Claude Code.
Runtime-fork prompts: paired divs, shared chip.
Runtime-mechanical scaffolding asymmetry — MORE in less-fluent fork, not less.
Append-vs-integrate — name integration mode on regeneration with new context source.
Citation discipline — extend cite-or-flag scope + quote supporting sentence.
Niceness tax — name the edge or pin the line on regeneration.
Question-dump default — `in turn` too soft; two legal shapes.
Overwrite anxiety — name overwrite default on regeneration.
Preamble before action — design around it.
Self-critique register, not defense, when Claude interrogates own work.
Minimal hand-off + Claude self-augments for send-off prompts.
Grill before save — collaborative quality at artefact assembly.
Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
Prompt-body edits require maintainer approval — registry files AND inline blocks.
Artifact destinations are explicit subpaths, never naked filenames (Agents 101-specific).
Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
`subagent` allowed in prompt blocks; explain why after prompt.
Maintainer-approval edits — ONE-AT-A-TIME, PRIORITY-ORDERED, FOUR-FIELD cards.
Name consumer at write time — `Save it as <path>` requires downstream reader.
Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `**Prompt**` — custom labels break renderer.
Normal work request before orchestration.
Live-test corrections preserve operator workflow.
Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
Module names in prompt prose are fine — they ground the session.
